newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares rebound on firm Flughafen demand.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares rebound on firm Flughafen demand.

text.p: Austrian shares closed firmer on Monday, boosted by record international leads and a rebound in shares of Vienna airport operator Flughafen after last week's bruising sell-off.
Strong demand for Flughafen and engineering group VA Technologie meant volumes were higher than they have been recently, they added.
The blue-chip ATX index closed up 1.10 percent at 1,023.38, just off the day's high of 1,024.18. Among its constituents 17 gainers outweighed four losers.
Traders said the market should see further gains over the rest of the week. They said the next target would be 1,040 points, which has offered stiff resistance for the last few weeks.
"The conditions are good and English investment banks have recommended a number of Austrian stocks as a buy," said one.

Flughafen was the top gainer, jumping 4.37 percent at 575 schillings on turnover of over 77,000 lots. The stock plunged as much as 22 percent last week on news of lower-than-expected first-half earnings.
Paper-maker Leykam was the leading decliner, slipping 1.02 percent to 292 schillings.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index inched up 0.72 percent at 400.42.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, ATX contracts for September delivery were up 12.0 points at 1,025 schillings ahead of Friday's expiry.
